messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 alert: gateway-proxy-eu-west-1 - 502 spike detected (12.4% 2m error rate). routing layer showing >50% of upstream failures as 'upstream prematurely closed connection' :rotating_light:

samir: I'm paged, jumping in. Priya, can you pull the edge metrics and confirm whether this is regional?

priya: looking now. dashboards show eu-west-1 only, small blip in us-east. latency also up ~200ms p95. customer-facing errors are coming from the /v1/generate and webhook ingestion endpoints.

migu el: fyi I saw a deploy to gateway routing rules ~15m ago (cfg: gateway-route-v2) by Drew. Could be related.

drew: I can confirm I rolled gateway-route-v2 18m ago; it touched header-based routing and new upstream pool weights. No DB/schema changes.

samir: ok let's treat as potential routing/regression. Priya, start isolating by host group. Miguel, can you check upstream pod restarts?

priya: query: `sum(rate(nginx_upstream_requests{status=502}[2m])) by (upstream)` shows majority from upstream=backend-embedding-eu-1.

miguel: checking nodes... backend-embedding-eu-1 pods show repeated `io timeout` and restarts around 2143204800. kube events show OOMKilled on one replica then flapping.

samir: immediate mitigation options: 1) shift traffic away from backend-embedding-eu-1 via routing weights, 2) scale up pool for that upstream, 3) rollback gateway-route-v2. Which is fastest?

drew: fastest is shifting weights or draining that upstream. I can push a temporary weight change to 0 for backend-embedding-eu-1.

emily: +1 for weight change, avoids risky rollback. Also start scaled replicas to replace OOM node.

priya: I'll kick a scale to +3 replicas for backend-embedding-eu-1: `kubectl scale deploy/embedding-eu --replicas=5 -n prod` and add alert to watch memory.

opsbot: action taken: scaled deployment embedding-eu -> replicas=5 (initiated by priya)

samir: Drew, apply weight 0 to backend-embedding-eu-1 and redistribute to backend-embedding-eu-2/3. Keep me posted.

drew: applying weight change now. command: `gatewayctl set-weight --upstream backend-embedding-eu-1 --weight 0 --commit`

incident-bot: deployment event: weight-change applied by drew at 2143205220

priya: traffic shift in progress. 502 rate dropping to 3.1% now. p95 latency trending down.

migu el: logs from backend-embedding-eu-1 show repeated `malloc` failures right before OOMs. Could be a memory leak in the model runner.

samir: good mitigation. Next we need an incident severity/impact summary for customer comms: who is impacted, scope, ETA for full recovery. Priya, quick estimation?

priya: Impact: ~8% of API requests globally saw error or timeouts in the last 10m but currently limited to EU region. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (batch inference) and webhook ingestion. Potentially affecting customers with EU-hosted workloads and high-concurrency embedding pipelines.

emily: current mitigation: traffic shifted; autoscaling kicked; error rate down to 1.2% and counting. Recommend keeping weight=0 on failing upstream until a stable replica is validated.

samir: agreed. Post-incident actions: 1) run heap dump on failing pod, 2) pin rollback of gateway-route-v2 for safe config, 3) run canary against embedding pool a/ b after fix. Owners: Miguel (heap dump + root cause), Drew (config roll or rollback), Priya (scaling + follow-up), Samir (incident lead).

drew: note: rolling back gateway-route-v2 would impact header-routing change; want to avoid if mitigation holds. I'll prepare a rollback patch but won't execute without ops lead signoff.

miguel: taking heap dump: `kubectl exec -it embedding-eu-pod-3 -- jmap -dump:live,format=b,file=/tmp/heap.hprof` -> copying to s3 `s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2143205123/heap.hprof`

opsbot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2143205123/heap.hprof

priya: monitoring note: set alert for 502 > 1% sustained for 5m in eu-west-1 and paging escalation to SRE lead.

incident-bot: note: paging suppressed (oncall already present)

samir: update for customer-facing comms: We should craft a short status message: what happened, current state, mitigation steps, ETA for full restore (TBD), and next update in 30m. Emily can you draft?

emily: taking it. Draft: "We observed elevated 502 errors from EU gateway due to one upstream pool experiencing memory issues. Traffic has been shifted and autoscaled; most services are recovering. We're investigating a root cause and will update within 30 minutes."

samir: send to #customers-ops for approvals before broadcast. Priya, please attach the runbook link and heap dump path.

priya: runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/gateway-502s ; heap dump link above.

drew: quick ask: after we confirm stable, we should run a canary with gateway-route-v2 disabled for embedding pool to ensure routing change isn't compounding things. I'll schedule a canary.

migu el: confirmed one problematic binary build (model-runner v1.4.2) is on the K8s image for embedding-eu-1; others are on v1.4.1. That suggests a bad image rollout to a subset. I'll open a review.

samir: excellent find. That explains why only a single upstream flapped. Action: mark as probable root cause: partial bad rollout of model-runner v1.4.2. Owners: Miguel (confirm), Drew (rollback if needed).

emily: status update posted to #customers-ops and scheduled next update at +30m.

incident-bot: status: mitigation applied, error rate decreased to 0.8% at 2143205610.

samir: for timeline and handoff: we'll keep the thread open for 1h. If stable after 30m, we'll move to follow-up and assign postmortem. Otherwise escalate to Sev3 execs.

priya: adding post-incident checklist items: image pinning, ensure canary coverage for gateway-route changes, add memory metric alert for model-runner.

miguel: pulling image digests and comparing: embedding-eu-1 used digest sha256:aaa... v1.4.2, others have sha256:bbb... v1.4.1. I'll prepare a CVE/rollback advisory if needed.

drew: I'll block v1.4.2 from rolling further and prepare rollback plan to v1.4.1 for embedding pool.

emily: customer comms updated: same message with note "no customer data exposure detected".

samir: thanks team. I'll file the incident ticket with severity, timeline, and owners. If anyone sees an uptick reset the channel. Otherwise keep monitoring.

incident-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2143205123 (owner: samir)

emily: leaving follow-up items in the ticket and pinging solutions for impacted customers.

samir: handing off monitoring to Priya for the next 45m. Priya, take messaging and ops. I'll remain the incident lead until we move to postmortem.

priya: acknowledged. keeping watch.

migu el: will analyze heap and image diffs and post findings in the ticket.

drew: will hold rollback toggle ready if heap analysis exposes regression.

incident-bot: thread closed for active updates; keep posting to the ticket for async follow-ups.
